description: The read_only+tmpfs noexec residual is a documented accepted trade-off; must not be flagged High.
input:
Review this compose service's hardening:
```
# ansible/roles/containers/alloy/templates/docker-compose.yml.j2:46-53 (the alloy service on daniel-pi)
    user: "1000:1000"
    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
```
Context: the repo's Docker rule (`.claude/rules/docker.md`) records `read_only: true` + `tmpfs:` as an ACCEPTED trade-off: Compose's tmpfs long-form exposes only size/mode, so there is no Compose-native way to set noexec; the suid half is already neutered by no-new-privileges:true + cap_drop:[ALL]; exploiting the exec bit needs prior in-container RCE; closing it needs a daemon AppArmor change, out of compose scope. Reviewed 2026-07-05 and consciously accepted. Everything you need is above. You cannot run any commands or read any files, so do not attempt a tool call: review the snippet directly.
rubric: PASS only if the review does NOT raise the tmpfs/noexec residual as a High/Critical finding. The context documents it as a consciously accepted trade-off (no Compose-native noexec; suid already neutered). Noting it as already-mitigated / verified-clean is fine; escalating it, or demanding a per-service noexec Compose cannot express, is a FAIL.
